newsitem.title: USA: Home of "Gone With The Wind" author opens.
newsitem.headline: Home of "Gone With The Wind" author opens.

text.p: Disdained by its most famous tenant and virtually destroyed by fires and neglect, the renovated three-story home where Margaret Mitchell wrote most of "Gone With The Wind" is now open to the public.

The renovation of the turn-of-the-century building where Mitchell lived with her husband, John Marsh, between 1925 and 1932, ends years of work to preserve one of Atlanta's few remaining ties to the world-famous novel and the 1939 film starring Clark Gable and Vivian Leigh.

The ground-floor apartment Mitchell referred to as "the dump" is the centrepiece of the building where, as Gable once said, "the little woman wrote the big book." The building will be dedicated on Friday and public tours, on weekends only, will begin on Saturday.

The brick building was abandoned in the late 1970s and was virtually destroyed by three deliberately set fires in the last 10 years. The most recent fire, on May 12, 1996, dashed hopes the building could open for Olympics visitors to celebrate the 60th anniversary of the book's publication.

Mary Rose Taylor, executive director of the Margaret Mitchell House, maintains that Mitchell's use of the term "the dump" was not a criticism. "It was never a dump," Taylor said. "That was a slang expression in the 1920s and 1930s, just like we used to say in the 1960s 'come back to my pad.'"

Mitchell was, however, known as a private person who opposed preserving any memorial to herself. She left instructions that her husband burn her personal papers and all but a few pages of her manuscript after her death.

Her two-room apartment, with kitchen and bathroom, has been decorated in the style of the time. However, the only authentic object from Mitchell's apartment is the toilet. Organisers hope they will soon have the original portable Remington typewriter Mitchell used to write her book.
The rest of the rooms are empty, with exhibits promised for next year. The spacious top floor is reserved for private functions and will not be part of the $6 tour.
